verdict.rationale: LangGraph is fundamentally code/API-first — graph construction, streaming, persistence, interrupts, and checkpoints are all exposed as Python/JS API calls (langgraph-docs-1, -6, -18, -24), and the Agent Server/CLI expose deploy and dev capabilities (langgraph-docs-23, -28, -29). However, the debugging/visualization layer (LangSmith Studio) offers trace visualization, state-transition inspection, and runtime metrics (langgraph-gh-10/11) with no evidence these are fully queryable via a documented API, and a probe for an OpenAPI spec returned 404s (langgraph-probe-3), while a community question raises uncertainty about production API deployment parity (langgraph-comm-7). Missing for 10: a documented OpenAPI/REST spec proving UI-equivalent API coverage, and explicit confirmation that Studio's visualization/tracing features are retrievable via API calls.
